leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Define a generic List<T> component with a type parameter to create reusable list structures.
Apply TypeScript generics to specify the type of items the List component will render.
Use the type parameter T to define the structure of props for the List component.
Implement array iteration to map through items and render each element in the list.
Construct JSX elements dynamically by passing item data to child components.
Utilize the key prop to assign unique identifiers to each rendered list item.
Invoke the List component with different data types to demonstrate its reusability.
Handle empty arrays by implementing conditional rendering to display fallback content.
Access item properties within the render logic using the type-safe generic parameter.
Modify the List component to accept additional configuration props while maintaining type safety.
Return structured JSX from the List component that renders a complete list UI.
Compare the generic List<T> implementation with non-generic alternatives to understand type safety benefits.
